thread:
devon: pushed a tiny Next starter (github.com/redwood/aeon-next-starter) that wires LangChain + a minimal eval harness. CI on edge target is flaky: auth 401s then an intermittent stream stall. anyone seen this pattern?

riley: can you paste the failing snippet?

devon: ```
Error: 401 Unauthorized - missing api key
 at fetch (/workspace/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/lib/fetch.js:12:9)
Retries exhausted
```

hana: quick thought: are you accidentally using NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY in server routes for simplicity? that breaks edge runtime and leaks keys to the browser.

devon: i did that to make the demo frictionless for new devs. guess that was dumb.

riley: yep that's it. server-only code must use REDWOOD_API_KEY (no NEXT_PUBLIC). For edge handlers prefer explicit Authorization header: `headers: { 'authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}` }`.

ops-bot: suggestion: add a pre-submit GH action that verifies no NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY usage in server folders. Would prevent this class of bug.

hana: also parity note: our JS SDK auto-retries idempotent generate calls; the minimal Python example in the repo currently lacks retries. For cross-lang samples include a small retry snippet and call out the difference in README.

devex-bot: recommended snippet to include in sample README:
```js
// tiny retry helper for demos
const client = new RedwoodClient({ retry: { retries: 3, backoffMs: 200 } })
```

riley: streaming hang: the sample uses `await client.generate()` which buffers the whole response. For edge streaming you should use the streaming iterator and flush chunks ASAP: `for await (const chunk of client.streamGenerate(...)) { res.write(chunk) }`. also set a keepalive or heartbeat to avoid proxy idle timeouts.

devon: i'll swap env usage, add the retry helper, and convert the demo to streamGenerate. i'll also add a tiny telemetry ping on first-run so we can see fresh failures.

ci-bot: Build queued for branch fix/aeon-starter-2712345678  tests pending.

hana: one more UX ask: add a one-line chooser in the console quickstart pointing to "aeon-next-starter (lite)" vs "aeon-next-starter (streaming)" so folks know which sample supports streaming/evals. cuts confusion for new signups.

devon: good idea — i'll include that in the PR description. thanks! :sparkles:
